highlights:
Global electricity demand is on track to grow 3.6% annually through 2030, roughly 50% faster than the previous decade, but the binding constraint on grid expansion is no longer permits or capital. It is people: 2.4 utility workers nearing retirement for every worker under 25 across advanced economies, with 56% of the US utility workforce carrying fewer than 10 years of service. For GPU cluster operators waiting on interconnection approvals, the queue problem is about to get worse before it gets better, and no amount of signed offtake agreements fixes a shortage of qualified linemen and substation engineers.

### H200 rental rates rise 14.4% to $3.09/GPU-hour as memory demand strengthens.

Global · ▲ Bullish · 4 Aug 11:21 UTC · Company/PR

H200 Neo-Cloud rental rates climbed from $2.70 per GPU-hour in May to $3.09 in July 2026, a 14.4% increase, while H100 rates rose 7.0% to $2.75, widening the H200 premium to 12.1% in July.

Why this matters: H200's 141 GB HBM3e memory commands a growing premium over H100's 80 GB, inference workloads are memory-bound and willing to pay for capacity; pricing divergence will reshape neocloud procurement decisions.

results.title: 难逃组装厂命运？AI服务器厂“艰难求生”，业内称显卡租赁价格较年初高点“腰斩”-36氪
highlights:
英伟达股价新高，AI服务器厂商遇冷，显卡租赁价腰斩。

本周英伟达股价刷新历史新高，黄仁勋在股东大会上最新表示推理需要更多算力。但与这一积极信号形成鲜明对比的是，AI服务器业内近期迎来一系列变动，宝德、思腾合力欲“卖身”A股，莲花控股（600186.SH）为盘活资产出售智算服务器。

财联社记者从业内采访获悉，受制于上游芯片技术门槛的提高，大部分AI服务器厂商“艰难求生”，最终或难逃组装厂的命运。同时，多位受访者坦言“现在算力市场比较难做”、“红利期过了”，算力资源信息共享平台柏林云负责人更对财联社记者表示，当前以H20为代表的显卡租赁价格相较年初高点已“腰斩”。

...

据前述算力从业者称，由于AI芯片技术门槛不断提高，叠加芯片原厂通过“捆绑销售”（注：如主板等），降低了AI服务器厂商的议价权、选择权，导致其形势日渐紧迫。

...

## “红利期过了”，显卡租赁价格年内“腰斩”

“算力需求降低了很多，H20租赁价格相比年初高点大概‘腰斩’。”柏林云负责人告诉财联社记者。

某模型厂商人士分析，降幅最大的是A系列的卡，一方面原因是随着新系列出现，A系列卡的使用场景越来越窄，市场对其价值的认定就会持续下行。

事实上，业内对于“卡过时了”的判断早已存在。5月曾有算力从业者告诉财联社记者，目前高端算力仍然奇缺，A、H系列将淘汰，市场需要Blackwell架构。

25日，莲花控股也发布了一则公告：为盘活闲置资产，提高资产运营效率，公司控股孙公司浙江莲花紫星智算科技有限公司拟出售4台智算服务器，合同金额为420万元。

对此有从业者分析，莲花控股的这一动作背后，除了为回流资金、降低包袱和历史负债，主要原因正是“卡过时了”。

针对价格走势，还有业内人士向财联社记者分析，目前AI应用市场的玩家主要是几家大厂，“一个市场的客户集中度足够高的时候，下游的议价权就会变强，从需求的角度也会把价格打下来。”

不过前述算力从业者也告诉财联社记者，今年截至目前颇受行业期待的重磅模型OpenAI GPT-5、DeepSeekR2仍未发布，导致了算力租赁端现阶段的低迷。

还有数据中心从业人士认为，算卡价格下滑是合理的，主要是受供需关系影响，“它本身不是个理财产品。”

results.title: Dwarkesh Patel warns compute prices will surge 10x — The Frontier
highlights:
- Falling token prices reflect smart software routing, not dying demand for artificial intelligence.
- Compute bottlenecks pushed spot GPU prices up 40 percent as top labs outbid rivals.
- Goldman Sachs projects AI infrastructure buildout costs will hit $1.1 trillion by 2027.

...

That explosion in agentic volume is running straight into a physical wall. Discussing the mechanics on the Dwarkesh Podcast, host Dwarkesh Patel explained that while AI lab revenues are growing tenfold annually, physical compute capacity expands only three times a year. Spot prices for compute have already jumped 40% since February. Google is reportedly paying SpaceX double the spot rate - roughly $900 million a month - to secure 110,000 GPUs.

Patel argued that hardware builders cannot simply manufacture their way out of this crunch. Moore’s Law now delivers just a 1.4x performance gain per cycle, and expanding silicon output requires scarce lithography machines from ASML. Meanwhile, AI hardware has already swallowed 86% of TSMC’s N3 wafer node allocation, leaving almost no consumer chip capacity left to cannibalize. The result is a brutal selection pressure where elite labs outbid minor startups for scarce silicon.

results.title: 2026 H1 GPU 租赁市场回顾：价格进入平台期，供给结构分化 — ComputeIndex 研究院 — ComputeIndex
highlights:
CGPI 综合指数回落 3.6%，国际 GPU 价格坚挺，国产算力持续走低——基于 ComputeIndex 独有价格数据的综合分析

综合多家研究机构和 ComputeIndex 独有数据，2026 H1 GPU 租赁市场正在经历一场静默但深刻的结构性转变——不是崩盘，而是分化。

...

NVIDIA 2026 年 Q2 财报显示，数据中心业务营收同比增长 85%，但增速较此前三个季度有所放缓。SemiAnalysis 在其 GPU 市场动态报告中指出，2023-2025 年的「GPU 稀缺溢价」正在消退，市场进入「效率定价」阶段。

ComputeIndex GPU Price Index (CGPI) 的走势印证了这一判断。CGPI 以 2026-07-01 为基期（=100），截至 8 月 6 日报 97.7，30 日内降幅 3.6%。这一降幅主要受国产算力产能释放驱动。

- •国际 GPU 子指数 CGPI-Intl 报 98.7，反映高端 GPU 需求刚性——与 NVIDIA 财报中「H200/B200 供不应求」的表述一致
- •国产 GPU 子指数 CGPI-Domestic 报 93.3，降幅 6.7%——TrendForce 数据显示 2026 Q2 国产 GPU 出货量同比增长 150%+
- •管制溢价比（CGPI-Premium）报 1.71x，较 2025 年高峰 3.5x 大幅回落——CSIS 分析认为「市场已结构性适应管制」

...

SemiAnalysis 供应链追踪显示，台积电 CoWoS-L 先进封装产能在 2026 Q2 达到 40K/月，较 Q1 提升 33%。这是 B200/B300 供给改善的核心驱动力。但 HBM3e（12-Hi 36GB）仍为瓶颈——SK 海力士产能要到 Q4 才能充分释放。

值得关注的一个信号：H100 与 A100 80G 的时租价差几乎消失（$3.16 vs $3.18）。TrendForce 分析认为，这反映了 AI 推理需求的爆发——A100 作为存量最多的 GPU，在大模型推理场景中的性价比优势突出，生命周期被大幅延长。

SemiAnalysis 的判断：H100 二手残值将在 2027 年底降至原价 40-50%。但 ComputeIndex 数据显示，A100 80G 价格坚挺表明上一代 GPU 不会快速出清——推理需求为其提供了价格支撑。

...

华为昇腾计算产业白皮书（2026）披露，昇腾 910B/910C 系列 2026 H1 出货量同比增长 150%+。TrendForce 数据显示，中国国产 AI 芯片市场份额从 2025 年的 12% 提升至 2026 H1 的 22%。

ComputeIndex 价格数据从市场端验证了这一趋势：昇腾 910B2（西部节点版本）时租 ¥1.74，较年初下降约 17%。西部地区（贵州、内蒙古）新建智算中心的集中交付，短期供给偏宽松。

...

综合主要研究机构的观点，我们梳理出 2026 H2 的三大共识与三大分歧：

- •【共识】GPU 租赁价格进入平台期（NVIDIA、SemiAnalysis、TrendForce 均持此观点）
- •【共识】Blackwell 架构 GPU（B200/B300）将在 2027 年成为市场主力
- •【共识】国产 GPU 份额将持续提升，短期价格承压
- •【分歧】美国出口管制是否会进一步收紧（高盛认为概率 30%，CSIS 认为概率 50%）
- •【分歧】HBM 供给瓶颈何时缓解（SK 海力士指引 Q4，但 SemiAnalysis 认为将延迟至 2027 Q1）
- •【分歧】推理需求增速能否弥补训练需求放缓（买方 vs 卖方观点差异明显）

ComputeIndex 视角：我们更关注一个研究机构较少讨论的结构变量——中国西部地区算力供给过剩的风险。贵州、宁夏等地的智算中心集中交付后，如果需求增速不及预期，可能触发一轮国产算力的价格战。

### 结论

综合 NVIDIA 财报、SemiAnalysis 供应链分析、TrendForce 出货数据与 ComputeIndex 独有价格指数，2026 H1 GPU 租赁市场的核心结论是「分化」：国际高端紧、中端松，国产整体宽松但高端紧缺。对于算力采购决策者，当前窗口期利于买方——价格下行提供了谈判筹码，但高端 GPU 的供给不确定性仍建议提前锁价锁量。

results.title: GPU Leases Are Rising While Model Prices Fall
highlights:
For three years the advice was simple: if the API bill hurts, rent GPUs and serve the model yourself. That advice is quietly inverting. Per-token prices keep falling, while the compute you would rent to escape them is getting more expensive — Nvidia announced roughly a 20% rise on H100 rentals, and AWS put up H200 instance prices in January for the first time in about two decades. Here is the break-even arithmetic, and the honest caveat that these rises come off a crashed base.

...

## What changed

- Nvidia announced an approximately 20% price increase for H100 rentals in 2026. That is a stated move on rental pricing, not a market observation.
- Separately, market H100 rental costs have climbed by nearly 40% since October 2025. Different measurement, different mechanism — this is what the market has actually done, not what anyone announced.
- Separately again, H100 one-year lease contract prices rose approximately 40% over five months into early 2026. That is the contract market, and it is the one that carries lock-in risk.
- AWS raised H200 GPU instance prices by 15% on 4 January 2026. The `p5e.48xlarge`, which carries eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs, went from $34.61 to $39.80 per hour. It was the first GPU price increase in roughly two decades and broke a twenty-year precedent of cloud prices only ever going down.
- All of it comes off a collapsed base. H100 rental rates fell from roughly $8 per hour at their 2023 peak to as low as $1 to $2 per hour through the 2024-2025 oversupply. By early 2026 rates were still down roughly 64% to 75% from launch-era highs. A 40% rise from $2 an hour is not a return to $8.

...

Both ends of that ladder are now moving, and they are moving in opposite directions. Labs have cut per-token prices repeatedly through 2026, so the top rung keeps getting cheaper. The rented compute on the bottom rung is getting dearer. The gap you were arbitraging is closing from both sides at once.

This is not a contradiction, and it is worth understanding why rather than treating it as an anomaly. A per-token API price is set in a competitive market by a small number of operators who pool every customer's traffic into one serving fleet. They run near-perfect utilisation because someone in the world is always sending a request, they amortise a single model over enormous aggregate volume, and several of them are willing to compress margin to hold share. A rented GPU is a scarce physical asset priced by supply and demand, and you pay for wall-clock hours whether you use them or not. Falling token prices are evidence of scale and competition at the serving layer. They are not evidence that the silicon underneath got cheaper.

...

| Option | Headline rate | Per GPU-hour | Basis / source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 on-demand, full market range | $1.49 – $6.98 / hour | $1.49 – $6.98 | Varies by provider and commitment; bulk of the market clusters $2–$4 |
| H100 on-demand, budget tier | — | ~$2.85 – $3.50 | Budget-tier service average |
| H100 entry rate | — | from ~$2.01 | Provider-dependent starting price |
| A100 entry rate | — | from ~$1.09 | Provider-dependent starting price |
| GCP H100, `a3-highgpu-8g` | $80 – $90 / hour (8 GPUs) | ~$9.00 – $11.50 | On-demand list |
| AWS H200, `p5e.48xlarge` | $39.80 / hour (8 GPUs), up from $34.61 | ~$4.98 (was ~$4.33) | 15% increase effective 4 January 2026 |
| AWS per-GPU on-demand | — | ~$12.29 | Separate measurement to the p5e figure above — different instance basis |
| H100 one-year lease contract | No public rate card | Direction only | Contract prices up ~40% over five months into early 2026 |
| Owned hardware, effective all-in | — | ~$2.50 – $4.00 | Hardware amortised over 3 years, plus colocation and power, at 70% utilisation |

Read that table twice. The two AWS rows and the p5e row are measuring different things and must not be merged into one number — the $39.80 figure is an eight-H200 instance after a specific 15% rise, while the roughly $12.29 per-GPU figure is a separate on-demand measurement on a different basis. Similarly, the three headline percentage rises at the top of this piece are three distinct measurements of three distinct markets. Anyone adding them together to claim GPUs got 100% dearer is doing arithmetic on numbers that do not belong to each other.

What the table does show unambiguously is a four-to-eight times spread on the same class of silicon. A team paying hyperscaler list rates and complaining about GPU inflation has a much larger and much easier saving available than anything leasing or owning will produce.

...

The most expensive mistake available in 2026 is signing a multi-year lease at the top of a rising market on a utilisation figure you have assumed rather than measured. One-year H100 lease contract prices rose roughly 40% over five months into early 2026 — a contract signed against that level is priced off a spike, not a trend, and you carry it for the full term. Meanwhile the on-demand market still spans $1.49 to $6.98 per hour depending on provider and commitment, so the supplier spread is frequently wider than the discount a lease buys. Before committing, measure four weeks of real utilisation from production telemetry. If it is not comfortably above 70% and stable, do not lock the term.

...

It also explains why GPU ... When compute was mostly a training cost, a 20% rise was a one-off hit to a budget line you had already ring-fenced. When compute is mostly an inference cost, the same 20% rise lands on a recurring, growing bill that sits directly against gross margin every month for the life of the product. And it explains why the market itself is being priced for growth: the AI GPU rental market was valued at $3.34 billion in 2023 and is projected to reach $33.91 billion by 2032. Suppliers are not pricing for a glut any more.

results.title: Reserve GPU Compute Now: Why Waiting Could Cost You 40% or More in 2026 | Source GPU
highlights:
H100 rental pricing rose almost 40 percent in five months. On-demand capacity is sold out across every major GPU type. If you're still waiting for a better moment to lock in compute, the data says that moment already passed. 

Waiting to reserve GPU compute used to be a reasonable bet. Prices moved slowly, capacity was generally available, and there was rarely a real cost to holding off a few more weeks before committing. That's no longer the market you're in.

...

H100 1-year reserved rental pricing climbed from roughly $1.70 per GPU-hour in October 2025 to $2.35 per GPU-hour by March 2026, an increase of almost 40 percent in five months. That's not a one-time correction. AWS raised H200 capacity-block pricing again in January 2026, this time by roughly 15 percent, with nothing in the underlying hardware or power cost changing at all. The increase was pure scarcity premium, providers charging more simply because demand for the same fixed supply kept climbing.

On-demand GPU rental capacity has been effectively sold out across every major chip type since early 2026. Teams that already hold on-demand instances aren't releasing that capacity back into the market even as prices rise around them, which means the squeeze isn't temporary friction, it's the market finding a new, higher equilibrium with less room in it than before.

...

The gap between reserved and on-demand pricing has widened into one of the clearest cost decisions in enterprise compute today. Long-term reservations commonly run 40 to 70 percent cheaper per hour than on-demand rates for the same hardware. Where on-demand H100 pricing hovers between $2.50 and $5.00 an hour depending on provider, reserved access to that same chip can bring the effective rate down to $1.00 to $2.00 an hour.

That spread exists because the on-demand price is effectively a queue price, what a provider charges when supply is genuinely scarce and demand is immediate. The reserved price is closer to the provider's actual supply forecast, discounted because they're getting certainty in exchange for a lower margin. In a market this tight, on-demand pricing captures the full scarcity premium every single hour. Reserving locks in a rate before the next price move happens, not after.

...

Rising prices are only half of what's driving urgency here. The other half is that reserving isn't only about the rate you lock in, it's about whether the capacity exists for you to reserve at all. As on-demand pools stay sold out and providers prioritize committed customers when allocating scarce supply, teams without a reservation in place risk not being able to get the chip they need on the timeline they need it, regardless of what they're willing to pay.

This is exactly the dynamic behind the HBM memory shortage driving the underlying GPU supply constraint industry-wide. Memory production is sold out through 2026 and constrained well into 2027, which means the capacity squeeze on rental markets isn't a short-term blip waiting to correct. Planning around current pricing and availability, rather than waiting for relief that most of the industry doesn't expect soon, is the more realistic approach.

...

| Factor | On-Demand | Reserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typical H100 rate | $2.50 to $5.00 per GPU-hour | $1.00 to $2.00 per GPU-hour |
| Availability risk | High, most pools are effectively sold out | Lower, capacity is allocated ahead of need |
| Price exposure | Full exposure to future scarcity premiums | Rate locked for the reservation term |
| Best for | Short, unpredictable, or bursty workloads | Sustained or planned workloads of known duration |

results.title: 【SMM Analysis】Domestic vs. Nvidia GPU Leasing: Annual vs. 3-5 Year Contracts Amid Supply and Demand Shifts - Shanghai Metals Market (SMM)
highlights:
In the same computing power leasing market, a clear dividing line in contract duration is emerging: the Huawei Ascend 910B/910C series is generally leased starting from one year in mainland China. NVIDIA H100/H200 leasing resources typically requires a minimum three-year lock-in contract, with concessions for a five-year contract still limited. Under export controls, computing power has shifted from a "commodity" to a "scarce resource“, contract duration is precisely the price of that scarcity.

...

There is a clear divergence in contract terms between domestic computing power leasing and Nvidia computing power leasing. Domestic servers can be rented on an annual basis, while Nvidia servers generally require a minimum of three-year fixed contracts.

Domestic cards fall into a "buyer’s market" : Ascend 910B2 sees high vacancy rates and lower quotations in some regions. Operators and lessors offer one-year short-term contracts in exchange for liquidity, reflecting typical oversupply pricing.

Imported cards fall into a "seller’s market" : For H100/H200, not only is the minimum lease term fixed, but a five-year fixed contract is only about 3,000–5,000 yuan/month cheaper than the three-year one (according to SMM sources) — if a buyer signs a five-year contract to save costs, the discount is not enough to cover the risk of the additional two-year lock-in period. The fact that buyers are willing to accept this just shows the core demand is "securing card access in the next five years," rather than price .

...

SMM Insight: From H100, H800 to H200, the supply of high-end cards to China over the past four years has been in a cycle of "control—tightening—limited clearance"; the "case-by-case review" for H200 also means that each shipment delivery is fraught with uncertainty. For lessees, if they don’t lock in resources today, they may not be able to purchase them tomorrow — this is the most fundamental supply-side logic behind 3-year/5-year fixed contracts.

...

Total intelligent computing capacity increased substantially : According to data disclosed by the MIIT on July 20, 2026, as of the end of June 2026, China’s intelligent computing capacity reached 2,185 EFLOPS (FP16) , up about 37% from approximately 1,590 EFLOPS at the end of 2025. Among this, the western region accounted for 32.6%, and the national computing facility utilization rate was 71.4%.

Scissors gap widens : According to data from CAICT, in Q1 2026, domestic AI computing demand surged 417% YoY , while supply growth was only around 128% — demand growth was about 3.3 times that of supply.

Structural gap : According to public industry estimates, the effective supply of high-end computing power required for long-cycle training of large models in China can only meet less than 47% of market demand, and the shortfall in high-end training computing power accounts for about 35% of effective demand.

SMM Insight: Nvidia GPU supply is locked by trade controls, while intelligent computing demand grew by 417%. The high-end computing power supply-demand gap is unlikely to close in the visible future of the next 3–5 years, which corresponds exactly to the lock-in periods of fixed contracts.

...

Now : The main battlefield has shifted to the upstream equipment suppliers in the supply chain — scheduling production, scrambling for quotas, sorting out high-end computing device channels, and locking in goods with server OEMs, corresponding to a market where high-end computing power is extremely scarce. At the same time, the computing power leasing transaction market is chaotic, lacking unified and standardized quotations; there are many intermediaries and agents in the industry. In a 200-person computing power leasing WeChat group with active transaction information, there are 76 intermediaries, accounting for as much as 38%. Identifying genuine computing power equipment supply channels that can directly connect to the cargo owner is also a difficulty in the daily work of operator managers. Public evidence is equally clear: the delivery lead time for domestic AI servers has stretched from an average of 4 weeks in 2025 to 16–20 weeks in Q2 2026—" running the supply chain" rather than " chasing clients"—the most authentic market footnote to tight server supply.

...

SMM believes: Nvidia GPU rentals commonly require three- or five-year closed-end contracts, which essentially establish a hedging and lock-in mechanism to cope with equipment supply shortages and tight supply under sanctions pressure —the lessee trades duration liquidity for “computing power availability + price certainty,” while the lessor locks in scarce capacity and stable cash flow through long-term agreements. Contract duration thus becomes the most direct gauge of high-end computing power scarcity. The key difference is that the one-year short contract for domestic cards reflects oversupply; Nvidia’s three-year closed-end contract embodies undersupply— the same contract terms write overcapacity on one side and supply chain crisis on the other . When contract duration begins to price the market, computing power leasing has already evolved from renting machines into a business model centered on resources, duration, and credit.

results.title: SpaceX's rapid expansion is consuming computing power! GPU shortage warning resurfaces for 2027: BNP Paribas sees CoreWeave (CRWV.US), Nebius (NBIS.US), and Oracle (ORCL.US) as the biggest potential winners | Bitget News
highlights:
Analyst Stefan Sławiński said, "As SpaceX publishes its first quarterly financial report as a publicly listed company, Musk has outlined an ambitious infrastructure roadmap, aiming to expand its AI compute footprint from approximately 2 GW at the end of 2026 to 'close to 10 GW rather than 5 GW' by the end of 2027. Combined with SpaceX repeatedly emphasizing its relationship with Nvidia, we're beginning to question whether GPU supply will once again become a key constraint for AI infrastructure deployment over the next 12 to 18 months, presenting both risks and opportunities."

...

SpaceX's aggressive capacity expansion (along with Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, Oracle, CoreWeave, and Nebius—a total of eight major players) is projected to drive an incremental AI demand of over 30 GW by 2027. However, the market's revenue expectations for Nvidia only correspond to a delivery capacity of 19 GW, indicating a supply gap of about 17%.

This means the situation of GPU undersupply may persist all the way through to after 2027. Against this backdrop, major clients with “priority allocation rights” for Nvidia hardware or in-house chip development capabilities will obtain substantial competitive barriers and excess market gains.

...

The analyst believes that SpaceX’s statements further confirm that shortages in AI computing power are unlikely to be alleviated, even by 2027. SpaceX management stated that memory output grows about 20% annually, while underlying AI demand is increasing by over 200%, meaning supply growth will consistently and significantly lag behind demand. Even if that direction is roughly correct, it indicates the currently favorable pricing environment is unlikely to normalize in the near term.

The analyst also considers it perhaps more significant that Musk speculated that systems based on the next-generation Vera Rubin architecture could eventually monetize $3 billion to $5 billion per GW, far surpassing previous industry expectations of $1.5 billion per GW.

...

For small and mid-sized cloud vendors lacking direct strategic agreements with Nvidia, or without in-house chip capabilities, the risks of supply disruption for chips and of stalled compute power deployments become even more severe.

On the supply side, growth (such as memory output increasing about 20% year-on-year) significantly lags behind demand (with underlying AI demand growing over 200% per year). This severe supply-demand imbalance means the current high-profit, strongly priced environment in the compute power market definitely won't subside or see price cuts any time soon.

results.title: 【SMM算力午评】4090长三角最低价上行，涨价行情由高端向主流全面铺开__上海有色网
highlights:
### 4090长三角最低月租升至7200元（涨2.86%）、最低卡时升至1.25元（涨2.46%），最低价上行预示低价货源收窄。涨价已由高端卡向主流消费级GPU全面铺开，算力资源价格持续上行，短期易涨难跌。

【市场概述】

今日上午长三角区域4090最低价出现上行。SMM-4090-24G-整机-长三角-包月最低月租从7000元升至7200元，折合最低卡时1.25元。与近期高端卡领涨不同，本轮涨价已传导至4090这一主流消费级算力——最低价抬升意味着低价货源正在收紧，算力资源价格上行呈全面铺开之势。

【4090长三角：最低价上行，价格底部抬升】

SMM-4090-24G-整机-长三角-包月最低月租从7000元升至7200元，上涨200元，涨幅2.86%；最低卡时从1.22元升至1.25元，上涨0.03元，涨幅2.46%。

最低价上涨具有信号意义：在算力资源整体紧缺的背景下，此前相对充裕的主流算力供给也在收窄，持货方惜售情绪由高端蔓延至中低端。长三角作为算力需求最密集的区域之一，4090整机低价货源被快速消化，价格底部被动抬升。

【SMM观点】

本轮上涨印证算力资源价格正处于持续上行通道。需关注两点：其一，涨价由高端（H100/H800）向主流消费级（4090）扩散，说明紧缺不再是高端专用市场的局部现象，而是整体供需失衡的全面反映，短期价格中枢易涨难跌。其二，对以4090为主要供给的中小需求方而言，最低价抬升直接推高算力成本，建议关注中长期租约以锁定成本、规避短期追涨。后续拐点仍取决于新增供给投放节奏与需求增速的相对变化。

results.title: Rising compute costs signal a strategic shift in the AI sector | Noah Intelligence
highlights:
The AI industry faces a new challenge as soaring GPU rental rates and infrastructure bottlenecks threaten profit margins, transforming compute access into a strategic battleground for leading firms.

The latest warning sign in the artificial intelligence boom is not a model failure or a chip shortage, but a squeeze on margins. Across the sector, the price of compute is rising fast enough to unsettle even the most confident backers, with GPU rental rates climbing sharply as demand for training and inference keeps outpacing supply. A July study by CCIR found that posted rental rates across several GPU generations have risen again since late 2025, while one-year H100 contracts have also surged, underscoring how quickly the economics of AI infrastructure are changing.

...

The wider industry is also starting to price in a world where the bottleneck is no longer simply “more chips”, but the ability to turn chips into useful throughput. CTAIO’s framework argues that power delivery, network design and scheduler maturity now matter as much as raw hardware availability, because under-used accelerators are an expensive form of dead capital. That is one reason the current compute squeeze feels so destabilising: the value chain is shifting from silicon ownership towards operational efficiency, and not every company is built to cope. 

If that holds, the implications go beyond higher cloud bills. A 40% rise in reserved GPU pricing over six months, reported in May 2026, suggests the market is already moving from plentiful capacity to rationed access. In practice, that could force AI companies to choose between thinner margins, higher prices for customers, or slower product roll-outs. The result is less a normal infrastructure cycle than a situational margin call on the entire AI sector.
